Quality.label: Quality
Quality.help: Resolution and ray-march steps of the fog pass

Temporal.label: Temporal filter
Temporal.help: History weight of the temporal filter, 0 = off

FogCeiling.label: Fog ceiling
FogCeiling.help: While you fly or stand well above the ground, the fog keeps to this many yards over the ground (fading over half as much again), so it lies in valleys and among the trees and the air above it is clear; the sunlit air still shows the shafts. It comes in as the camera rises from 1.5 to 3 times this height over the ground under it, so nothing changes on foot. 0 = off

Haze.label: Haze
Haze.help: Distance haze where no Classic data exists

GroundFog.label: Ground fog
GroundFog.help: Low ground mist where no Classic data exists

FarFog.label: Distance fog
FarFog.help: The distance fog that replaces the stock fog

FarFogStretch.label: Fog follows the view
FarFogStretch.help: 1: with the view distance lifted past the client's cap, the distance fog reaches as much further as the view does, so land past the zone's fog end is not drawn as a flat fog-coloured shape. 0: the fog ends at the zone's fog distance in yards

AerialPerspective.label: Aerial perspective
AerialPerspective.help: 1: distant land fades into the zone's own fog colour, the sky at the horizon, and the sun brightens the haze only around itself. 0: the haze is lit by the sun from every side, which turns distant mountains pale

StockFog.label: Replace the stock fog
StockFog.help: On: the volumetric distance fog replaces the client's linear fog. Off: keep the stock fog

DataMode.label: Classic fog layers
DataMode.help: Use the Classic client's fog layers where its lights cover the map. Off: derived layers everywhere

MaxDistance.label: Fog range
MaxDistance.help: How far sky rays are integrated and the scale of the Classic distance curves

SunScatter.label: Sun scatter
SunScatter.help: In-scattered sun or moon light: the halo and the shafts

Exposure.label: Exposure
Exposure.help: Brightness of the layers used where no Classic data exists

ClassicExposure.label: Classic exposure
ClassicExposure.help: Brightness of the Classic layers, 1 = as authored

ColorSpace.label: Linear light
ColorSpace.help: Scatter and blend in linear light like the modern client, with a soft highlight roll-off. Off: gamma

LightShafts.label: Light shafts
LightShafts.help: Shadowed in-scattering: light shafts through trees, buildings and terrain

TerrainShadows.label: Terrain shadows
TerrainShadows.help: Mountains and buildings around you keep the sun and moon out of the fog in their shadow, whether or not they are on screen

SurfaceShadows.label: Surface shadows
SurfaceShadows.help: Shadows of mountains and buildings on the ground, walls and characters, from the same height map, whether or not the mountain is on screen. 1 = the sun's whole share of the light is taken away, 0 = off

LowSunLight.label: Low sun light
LowSunLight.help: While the sun is low, slopes and walls facing it, where it reaches, get a warm lift in its colour, so the light lands on the far mountains at dawn and dusk. 1 = 35% brighter, 0 = off

GodRays.label: God rays
GodRays.help: Radial rays from the bright sky around the sun, 0 = off

GlowCompensation.label: Glow compensation
GlowCompensation.help: Pre-compensate the fog for the client's full-screen glow, which otherwise bleaches bright fog around the sun to white

LightSaturation.label: Light saturation
LightSaturation.help: Colour of the sun's or moon's light in the fog, the shafts and the haze, at the same brightness: 1 = the client's, 0 = white. The sky-lit part of the fog keeps its colour

HazeSaturation.label: Haze saturation
HazeSaturation.help: Colour of the sky-lit part of the fog and the haze, the zone's fog colour, at the same brightness: 1 = the client's, 0 = grey, 2 = twice as strong

Saturation.label: Saturation
Saturation.help: Colour of the whole picture at the same brightness: 1 = unchanged, 0 = grey (needs Linear light)

SkySaturation.label: Sky saturation
SkySaturation.help: Colour of the sky alone, on top of Saturation: 1 = as the rest of the picture, 0 = grey

Temperature.label: Temperature
Temperature.help: White balance of the whole picture at the same brightness: above 0 warmer (amber), below 0 cooler (blue); 1 = red twice blue (needs Linear light)

Tint.label: Tint
Tint.help: White balance of the whole picture at the same brightness: above 0 toward magenta, below 0 toward green (needs Linear light)

SkyTemperature.label: Sky temperature
SkyTemperature.help: Temperature of the sky alone, on top of Temperature: 0 = as the rest of the picture

SkyTint.label: Sky tint
SkyTint.help: Tint of the sky alone, on top of Tint: 0 = as the rest of the picture

LightBalance.label: Light balance
LightBalance.help: White balance of the land and everything on it against the client's sun and ambient light: 0 = the client's colour, 1 = a neutral light at the same brightness, 2 = past it. Not the sky, not indoors (needs Linear light)

LandBrightness.label: Land brightness
LandBrightness.help: Brightness of the land and everything on it, not the sky: 1 = the client's (needs Linear light)

SkyBrightness.label: Sky brightness
SkyBrightness.help: Brightness of the sky alone, in linear light: 1 = the client's, 2 = twice as bright (needs Linear light)

SkyHaze.label: Sky haze
SkyHaze.help: Share of the clear sky behind a haze in the horizon's colour, as rain covers it with Overcast sky: 0 = the client's sky, 1 = all haze

SkyHazeGlow.label: Sun in the haze
SkyHazeGlow.help: Brightness of the sun's disc and its halo in the sky haze, in the sun's colour

SkyHazeZenith.label: Haze overhead
SkyHazeZenith.help: Brightness of the sky haze straight overhead against the horizon, in linear light: 1 = even, 0.1 = a bright band at the horizon under a dark sky

SkyHazeGlowGrade.label: Sun takes the sky's colour
SkyHazeGlowGrade.help: How much of the sky's own colour, brightness and saturation the sun's glow in the haze takes: 1 = all of it, 0 = it keeps the sun's colour under a sky turned cool or grey

HazeFromSky.label: Haze takes the sky's colour
HazeFromSky.help: How far the haze's sky-lit light in front of the land takes the colour of the sky at the horizon, as drawn: 1 = all the way (a bright sky gives bright distant hills, a dark one dark ones), 0 = the haze's own colour. The sky and the sun's light in the haze are unchanged

HazeSkyLevel.label: Haze against the sky
HazeSkyLevel.help: The brightness of that haze against the sky at the horizon, as displayed: 0.85 = a bit darker, 1 = as bright. Land seen through the haze keeps some of its own light, so snow can still stand out brighter than the sky

Shafts.label: Shafts
Shafts.help: Extra sunlight scattered in the fog and the air wherever the sun reaches, traced through trees, buildings and terrain whether or not the sun is on screen. 0 = only the fog's own shadowed light

ShaftFocus.label: Focus
ShaftFocus.help: 0 = shafts as bright from every side; higher = brighter looking toward the sun, fainter looking away

LowSunShafts.label: Low sun
LowSunShafts.help: Stronger shafts while the sun is low: 1 = twice as strong at dawn and dusk, fading out by 30 degrees up; 0 = the same all day

ShaftGlare.label: Sun glare
ShaftGlare.help: How bright the shafts' light grows before it grows only slowly: lower keeps the glow around a low sun small while beams through trees and gaps keep their strength; 4 = almost no limit

MoonShafts.label: Moon shafts
MoonShafts.help: The same beams from the moon at night. Moonlight is dim and the moon stands high, so they need more strength than the sun's. 0 = only the fog's own shadowed light

MoonShaftFocus.label: Moon focus
MoonShaftFocus.help: Focus of the moon's shafts. The moon stands high, so a low focus keeps them visible when looking level

ShaftHaze.label: Clear air
ShaftHaze.help: Air lit by the shafts, so they show where the fog is thin

ShaftRange.label: Range
ShaftRange.help: How far from the camera shafts are traced

ShaftMemory.label: Remember what was seen
ShaftMemory.help: Trees and buildings shade the shafts from a shadow map, seen from the sun, of everything the camera has seen so far. It stays fixed in the world, so turning the camera does not change the shafts, and gaps between leaves stay open. Off = only what is on screen, with a guess past its edges

ShaftLength.label: Length
ShaftLength.help: How far toward the sun each point looks for trees and buildings that shade it (only without the memory, which looks all the way)

ShaftDepth.label: Occluder depth
ShaftDepth.help: How deep trees and buildings are taken to be behind their visible face, per yard of their distance (only without the memory)

Drift.label: Drift
Drift.help: How patchy the fog is. The patches drift with the wind and the shafts brighten in the thick ones. 0 = even fog, as before

DriftSize.label: Patch size
DriftSize.help: Size of the drifting fog patches

DriftDetail.label: Smoke
DriftDetail.help: Share of fine, wispy smoke in the drift, a tenth of the patch size and smaller. 0 = only the large patches

DriftSwirl.label: Swirl
DriftSwirl.help: How far the large patches twist and stretch the smoke. 0 = straight wisps

Banks.label: Fog banks
Banks.help: Gathers the fog into separate banks, as big as the patches, that lie on the ground, fill valleys and leave clear air between them, instead of even layers at your own height

options.label: Valleys and water at dawn and dusk

BankCover.label: Bank cover
BankCover.help: Share of the ground under a fog bank; the banks are denser where they are fewer, so the fog as a whole keeps its amount. 1 = one even blanket

BankHeight.label: Bank height
BankHeight.help: How high the banks reach above the ground under them

BankPool.label: Valleys
BankPool.help: How much the fog gathers in valleys and over lakes and leaves ridges and hilltops clear. 0 = the same on every slope

BankShadow.label: Bank shade
BankShadow.help: How much a bank shades its own inside from the sun or moon, so it has a lit side and a dark one

StormWind.label: Storm wind
StormWind.help: Drift speed in full rain, snow or sandstorm; weaker weather lies in between

WindDirection.label: Wind direction
WindDirection.help: Where the wind blows to: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west

MorningMist.label: Morning mist
MorningMist.help: Extra fog in low ground at dawn (full 05:00 to 07:30, gone by 10:00). 2 = three times the fog near the ground; zones with little fog of their own get up to eight times more

MistHeight.label: Mist height
MistHeight.help: How far above your ground level the morning mist reaches

EveningHaze.label: Evening haze
EveningHaze.help: Extra fog everywhere in the evening (full 20:00 to 22:00, gone by midnight)

WeatherFog.label: Weather fog
WeatherFog.help: Extra fog in full rain, snow or sandstorm. 1 = twice the fog

WeatherShafts.label: Weather shafts
WeatherShafts.help: Share of the shafts left in full weather, as clouds hide the sun

WeatherTint.label: Weather tint
WeatherTint.help: Fog turns grey in rain, white in snow and sandy in a sandstorm

WeatherSky.label: Weather sky
WeatherSky.help: The sky and its clouds turn the colour of the weather's fog, overcast. 1 = 85% in full weather

RainInFront.label: Rain in front
RainInFront.help: Rain, snow and sand stay in front of the fog and the overcast sky, as near as they fall: 1 = fogged as if 25 yd away, 0 = as if as far as what is behind them

DustHaze.label: Dust haze
DustHaze.help: Warm, sunlit dust in the air of dry zones, thickest in the afternoon and in wind. 0 = off

HumidHaze.label: Humid haze
HumidHaze.help: A soft, cool haze over green open land, thickest in the morning. 0 = off

HorizonFog.label: Horizon fog
HorizonFog.help: In dry and green zones, far land fades gradually into the colour of the sky at the horizon. 0 = the zone's own distance fog

CloudShadows.label: Cloud shadows
CloudShadows.help: Shadows of clouds drifting with the wind over dry and green zones, on the ground and in the haze; with a low sun they give beams between the clouds. 1 = a cloud takes the sun's whole share of the light away, 0 = off

CloudCover.label: Cloud cover
CloudCover.help: How much of the sky the clouds cover: 1 = about a quarter in dry zones and nearly half in green ones, at most 90%

CloudSize.label: Cloud size
CloudSize.help: How wide one cloud is, in yards

Twilight.label: Twilight
Twilight.help: Blue tint of the fog around sunset and sunrise, while the sun is just below the horizon and the moon is not up

SkyboxMoons.label: Skybox moons
SkyboxMoons.help: Draw the moons the HD skyboxes paint on their sky. Off = only the game's own moon shows, the one the moonlight, the moon shafts and the glitter on the water come from

SunAndMoon.label: Sun and moon over the sky
SunAndMoon.help: The game's own sun and moon drawn over the sky last, so an HD skybox or the sky haze cannot hide them; land in front still does. 1 = as the client draws them, dimmer in thick fog and rain; 0 = left to the client, under the skybox and the haze

LightGlow.label: Light glow
LightGlow.help: Lamps, windows and fires glow into the fog at night; the thicker the fog, the larger the halo. 0 = off

GlowThreshold.label: Glow threshold
GlowThreshold.help: How bright a pixel must be to glow; lower = more things glow

LampFog.label: Lamp halos
LampFog.help: Torches, candles, braziers and lanterns placed in the world glow in the air, more in rain, snow or sand; by day the By day share of it; none in the ghost world. Needs lampdata.bin. 0 = off

LampCount.label: Lamps
LampCount.help: How many lamps in view glow and light things, brightest first. Lamps reach 800 yd and fade from 650 yd; while halos or far lights show, up to 64 more lamps beyond 80 yd glow without lighting things

LampFlicker.label: Flicker
LampFlicker.help: How much flames flicker; lanterns behind glass stay steady. 0 = steady

FireStrength.label: Fires
FireStrength.help: Strength of open fires (braziers, bonfires, campfires and hearths), their light and halos, against the other lamps. 1 = as the other lamps

FarLights.label: Far lights
FarLights.help: At night the lamps of towns and camps from 60 yd out show as small points of light, even where their halos are too faint to see, so a town across a valley isn't dark. Hidden lamps show none. 0 = off

LampIndoors.label: Indoors
LampIndoors.help: Strength of lamps inside rooms (inns, houses, halls), and of every lamp while you stand indoors, their light and halos. 1 = as outdoors

LampLight.label: Lamp light
LampLight.help: The same lamps light the ground, walls, plants and characters around them in their own colour, falling off like the game's own lights; by day too, most in shade; none in the ghost world. 0 = off

LampDayLight.label: By day
LampDayLight.help: Share of the lamps' light and halos by day, when the sun outshines them. 0 = none by day, 1 = as at night

WindowLight.label: Window light
WindowLight.help: Lit windows cast their light onto the street, walls and characters in front of them, up to 8 windows at a time; none by day and none in the ghost world. 0 = off

EffectLight.label: Spell light
EffectLight.help: Glowing spells, projectiles, enchants and other bright effects on screen light the ground, walls and characters around them in their own colour, up to 6 at a time; the placed lamps' own flames are left to the lamps. In rain or snow only coloured glows count. By day the lamps' By day share; none in the ghost world. 0 = off

ObjectLamps.label: Game object lamps
ObjectLamps.help: Campfires, braziers, candles and torches the server places (cooking fires, camps, festival braziers) light and glow like the lamps of the world, where they stand, from the client's own list of objects. Needs lampdata.bin from this version's Lumenveil-Setup.cmd. Off = they only give spell light

CorpseLight.label: Loot sparkle
CorpseLight.help: Corpses you can loot give a small golden twinkle of light, the nearest 4 within 40 yd, from the client's own list of what is lootable. By day the lamps' By day share; none in the ghost world. 0 = off

LampShadows.label: Lamp shadows
LampShadows.help: Things on screen between a lamp and a surface block its light. 0 = no lamp shadows

CarriedShadows.label: Carried light shadows
CarriedShadows.help: How much of the lamp shadows the lights that move with things keep: spells, projectiles, enchants, the loot sparkle and the belt lantern. 0 = they cast no shadows, so no character's shadow swings around with them; placed lamps keep theirs

NightDarkness.label: Night darkness
NightDarkness.help: Darkens the moonlit scene at night outdoors, but not flames, lit windows, lit interiors or what the lamps light, and not while you are indoors. 0 = the game's own night

Lantern.label: Lantern
Lantern.help: A lantern at your belt lights the ground, walls, plants and characters around you, and what stands in its light casts shadows. In the dark it lights by itself at night and indoors (caves, dungeons, buildings) and goes out by day; never while swimming or as a ghost

LanternLight.label: Lantern light
LanternLight.help: How brightly the lantern lights things around you. 0 = no lantern

LanternHalo.label: Lantern halo
LanternHalo.help: How strongly the lantern glows in the fog around it, on top of Lamp halos. 0 = no glow

LanternSwing.label: Swing
LanternSwing.help: How much the lantern swings on its hook as you walk, run, turn and stop. 0 = it hangs still

Relief.label: Relief
Relief.help: Paved roads, tiles, stones and rock on the ground get depth: they shift with the view (parallax occlusion), catch the light on their sunlit side and shade themselves. Needs reliefdata.bin and exterior shadows 3-5 (extShadowQuality)

ReliefModels.label: On models
ReliefModels.help: Trees, creatures, characters, armour and props get relief too. Their height maps are made while you play, on a thread of their own, the first time each texture is drawn

ReliefDepth.label: Depth
ReliefDepth.help: How deep the relief is at its deepest, for stone and paving; each texture type gets its share of it (Relief by texture type)

ReliefLight.label: Light
ReliefLight.help: How strongly the relief shapes the light (its sunlit and shaded sides). 0 = depth only

ReliefShadows.label: Self shadows
ReliefShadows.help: How dark the shadows are that stones and ridges cast onto their own texture

ReliefDistance.label: Distance
ReliefDistance.help: Relief is drawn up to this distance and fades out over its last quarter

ReliefRoads.label: Roads
ReliefRoads.help: Roads, paving, cobbles and paved floors, outdoors and in buildings

ReliefRock.label: Rock
ReliefRock.help: Rock, cliffs, gravel, boulders and caves

ReliefDirt.label: Dirt
ReliefDirt.help: Dirt, mud, soil, ash, and ground of no other type

ReliefGrass.label: Grass
ReliefGrass.help: Grass, moss, fallen leaves and crops on the ground

ReliefWalls.label: Walls
ReliefWalls.help: Walls of stone, brick and plaster, trim, pillars, ceilings and window frames

ReliefWood.label: Wood
ReliefWood.help: Planks, beams, wooden walls and floors, fences, crates and barrels

ReliefMetal.label: Metal
ReliefMetal.help: Metal and iron, chains, pipes and machines

ReliefBark.label: Bark
ReliefBark.help: Tree trunks, branches, roots and logs

ReliefLeaves.label: Leaves
ReliefLeaves.help: Leaves, bushes, plants and flowers on models

ReliefCharacters.label: Characters
ReliefCharacters.help: Characters and the armour they wear on their body

ReliefProps.label: Props
ReliefProps.help: Props: cloth, banners, lamps, signs and everything else

WaterReflect.label: Reflections
WaterReflect.help: Water mirrors the sky, shores, trees and buildings on screen; strong when you look across the water, weak when you look down into it. 0 = off

WaterGlitter.label: Glitter
WaterGlitter.help: Sparkling path of the sun, and of the moon at night, on the waves; less under clouds and none in the ghost world. 0 = off

WaterClarity.label: Clarity
WaterClarity.help: See the bottom through shallow water, and a deeper teal where the water gets deep. 0 = the game's own water colour

WaterSmooth.label: Smooth
WaterSmooth.help: The game's animated water texture under the reflections is replaced by the zone's own water colours, shallow to deep, rivers and lakes apart from the sea, so the water reads as one smooth surface that the waves and reflections play on. 0 = the game's texture as drawn

WaterBump.label: Bump
WaterBump.help: Fine ripples from the later clients' water normal map (waterbump.blp, copied from the game's archives by Lumenveil-Setup.cmd) drift with the wind over the waves and bend the reflections. 0 = off

WaterFoam.label: Foam
WaterFoam.help: Foam where the water is shallow along the shores, from the later clients' foam texture (waterfoam.blp, copied by Lumenveil-Setup.cmd), drifting with the wind. 0 = off

WaterWaves.label: Waves
WaterWaves.help: Small waves that break up the reflections and the glitter; higher in rain, snow or sand. 0 = a still mirror

WaterRain.label: Rain rings
WaterRain.help: How strongly raindrops ring out on the water while it rains; how many follows the rain. None in snow or sand. Far away they roughen the water instead. 0 = off

WaterMemory.label: Remember what was seen
WaterMemory.help: Reflections of what left the screen come from a panorama of everything seen from here, so turning the camera does not make them pop or vanish. Off = only what is on screen

SurfaceSheen.label: Sheen
SurfaceSheen.help: Stone, cobbles, rock, ice and other smooth surfaces catch the sun, the moon and the lamps when you look along them toward the light, most of all under a low sun; snow sparkles; grass, dirt and sand stay matt. 0 = off

WetSurfaces.label: Wet in rain
WetSurfaces.help: Rain wets what stands under the open sky within about a minute, each ground as its material takes water: stone gets a glossy film at once, soil and sand darken first, grass beads into droplets that glint but never mirror, snow does not darken. It dries over minutes once the rain stops, slower at night. Nothing under roofs. 0 = never wet

Puddles.label: Puddles
Puddles.help: How much of the flat open ground pools into puddles in steady rain: still mirrors that fill over a minute or two and outlast the wet ground. Never on grass or snow. 0 = no puddles

TerrainMaterials.label: Ground materials from textures
TerrainMaterials.help: Tell the ground's material from its texture (materialdata.bin): grass, soil, stone, sand, snow, ice, wood or lava. Off = judge every surface by its colour. Needs extShadowQuality 3+

Underwater.label: Fog under water
Underwater.help: Keep the effect while the camera is under water

LiquidDepth.label: Water writes depth
LiquidDepth.help: Let water surfaces write depth so water is fogged by its own distance

FarClipMax.label: View distance
FarClipMax.help: The client caps the continents at 791 yd; the engine allows 1583. Costs about four times the loaded terrain. 0 keeps the client's cap. Turning it on when it was off at start-up needs a client restart

DebugView.label: View
DebugView.help: Show one input of the fog instead of the scene

SunMarker.label: Sun marker
SunMarker.help: Red marker where the sun direction projects on screen

ClientShadowMaps.label: Client shadow maps
ClientShadowMaps.help: Find the client's own sun shadow maps each frame and describe them in CoAVolFog.log

DrawLog.label: Draw log
DrawLog.help: Draw log for research: 1 = DrawLogKey captures the next frame that draws the world to CoAVolFog-draws.csv next to the log (the key needs Overlay=1); 2 = the same once each time this file is read with DrawLog=2; 0 = off

PerfLog.label: Timing log
PerfLog.help: Frame profile: 1 = the main thread's and the GPU's time for each part of the fog, the client and Present, in the log every 60 s; 0 = off

DrawLogVertexConstants.label: Draw log vertex constants
DrawLogVertexConstants.help: Shader constants whose values the draw log writes to CoAVolFog-draws\constants.csv, as registers like c2-5,c37-48 (none = no values). Empty = vertex c0-7,c14-16,c31-33,c37-48,c224-235 and pixel c0-12, which cover the client's shadow-map matrices

DrawLogPixelConstants.label: Draw log pixel constants
DrawLogPixelConstants.help: Shader constants whose values the draw log writes to CoAVolFog-draws\constants.csv, as registers like c2-5,c37-48 (none = no values). Empty = vertex c0-7,c14-16,c31-33,c37-48,c224-235 and pixel c0-12, which cover the client's shadow-map matrices

Enable.label: Lumenveil
Enable.help: Off: the game is drawn as without Lumenveil, which stays installed. Needs a client restart

PlainGame.label: Plain game
PlainGame.help: On: the game is shown without Lumenveil, as the compare key shows it, at once and at every start. Off: Lumenveil is shown

EngineHooks.label: Engine hooks
EngineHooks.help: The hooks into the client that give the lamps, water, relief, shadows and lifted view distance. Off leaves only the fog. Needs a client restart

Overlay.label: Settings window
Overlay.help: The in-game settings window and the keys below. Turning it on again needs a client restart

OverlayKey.label: Settings window
OverlayKey.help: Shows and hides the in-game settings window

ToggleKey.label: Compare with the plain game
ToggleKey.help: Switches the whole mod off and on while you play, to compare with the plain game. Never saved

LanternKey.label: Belt lantern
LanternKey.help: Switches the belt lantern on or off and saves that

ReliefKey.label: Ground relief
ReliefKey.help: Switches the ground relief on or off and saves that

SpotKey.label: Save a spot
SpotKey.help: Writes where you stand, the time and the weather to CoAVolFog-spots.txt, to report a place that looks wrong

RegionKey.label: Zone looks window
RegionKey.help: Shows and hides the window of the looks kept per zone (CoAVolFog-regions.ini)

DrawLogKey.label: Draw log
DrawLogKey.help: Writes one frame's draw calls to the log, for debugging

ZoneDensity.label: Density per zone
ZoneDensity.help: Density per zone: the zone's id and a multiplier of Density, comma-separated (148:0.5,490:0.7), or none. The settings window's "Density" section sets the zone you stand in; a zone change fades over 4 seconds (0-4 each)

DryZones.label: Dry zones
DryZones.help: The zones that count as dry and as green, by the client's zone id, comma-separated, or none. CoAVolFog.log names the zone you enter, and the settings window's "Open land" section moves the zone you stand in between the lists

GreenZones.label: Green zones
GreenZones.help: The zones that count as dry and as green, by the client's zone id, comma-separated, or none. CoAVolFog.log names the zone you enter, and the settings window's "Open land" section moves the zone you stand in between the lists
